item.title: RSC Anderlecht: Purple, pop culture and a park
item.description: RSC Anderlecht: Purple, pop culture and a park Opposition analysis This Thursday 5 November our Red Bulls face one of the most exciting away trips on their UEFA Europa League fixture list. With 34 league titles and several European trophies to their name, Royal Sporting Club Anderlecht are not only the undisputed biggest name in Belgian football. The club also embodies, perhaps more than any other in Europe, a unique balance between a regal footballing past and an avant-garde present. 1908 year of foundation Between red brick and floodlights The match will take place at Lotto Park - a venue still known to many European football romantics by its historic name, the Constant Vanden Stock Stadium. Located in the heart of the lush Astrid Park in the Brussels suburb of Anderlecht, the arena has a capacity of approximately 21,500 spectators. What makes this place so special is its deep connection to the surrounding neighbourhood. The stands are positioned so close to the surrounding terraced houses that one corner of the stadium even had to be cut off diagonally to avoid obstructing the street. 106 Million Euro estimated market value On match days, the area around the stadium is filled with the scent of classic Belgian fries and light-coloured beer. In the neighborhood’s long-established pubs, portraits of legends - such as Henri Meert, Jan Mulder and homegrown talent Romelu Lukaku - hang on the walls. Jerseys from a pop star, football as haute couture The fact that the Mauves et Blancs (Purples and Whites) place great importance on their appearance has always been part of the club's identity. In recent years, the club has partnered with the Brussels-based fashion label Mosaert - a venture spearheaded by none other than global superstar Stromae , alongside designer Coralie Barbier and Luc Van Haver. Together, the collective gave the team’s kits and overall visual identity an elegant makeover, and they even produced a remix of the club anthem. On the banks of the canal Our team are heading to a capital defined by fascinating contrasts. On one side lies Brussels’ glamorous city center, home to the magnificent Grand Place, the royal galleries, and the world of international diplomacy. On the other side, west of the canal, pulses the authentic, gritty heart of Anderlecht, where the club remains deeply rooted in the daily life of the neighbourhood. On Thursday, it will be crucial for our boys to prevent the hosts from finding their rhythm on the pitch and to proactively silence the intense atmosphere at Astrid Park by imposing our own dynamic style of play! Fans following from home can catch the action via a stream on Canal+ with the match starting at 18:45 CET.

item.title: ‘Absolute disaster’ – Dave Portnoy explains why Angel Reese is to blame for Dream’s WNBA Finals loss
item.description: Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Dave Portnoy has hit out at Angel Reese for a ‘total disaster class’ in the last three games of the WNBA Finals. Media personality Dave Portnoy claims Angel Reese lost the WNBA Finals for the Atlanta Dream, pointing to her poor shooting statistics and low scoring. Reese began the WNBA Finals well. She scored 18.3 points per game over the first four. But at crunch time, in Games 5, 6, and 7, Reese’s output dipped to 10.0 PPG. This ended with only 8 points in the deciding game, won 68-63 by the Golden State Valkyries. Portnoy told Barstool Sports that he does not regard Reese as a top superstar, and blames her for the Atlanta Dream failing to win the title. He said: “In their last three losses, she scored 23 points, seven of 27 from the field. That’s 25 percent. Eight to 13 from the free throw line. You can sculpt this any way you want. In the last three losses that they had, she didn’t show up at all. Not even a little bit. Not even a tiny bit. “She made the finals. Congrats! But she lost them the Finals. There’s absolutely no other way to extrapolate this. “And good season, but before we start putting her in Caitlin Clark’s category to have three games held under 10 and just be a turnover machine, terrible at the line, there’s no other way to look at it. A total disaster class from Angel Reese.” Angel Reese is taking a break Angel Reese said the Atlanta Dream had been ‘delayed and not denied’, as she reacted to the team falling narrowly short in Game 7. And while her performances are dissected, she plans to take a break during the offseason. Posting on Instagram , she said she feels ‘numb’ after the loss but thanks the Atlanta Dream fans and community for their support. She added: “Atlanta, you’ve meant the world to me in just 7 months. I pray I get to experience this kind of joy forever. ♥️ “Back to work! See y’all in 6 months.” Read more: Why Angel Reese is still ‘numb,’ but ‘proud’ after Atlanta Dream’s 2026 WNBA Finals defeat ‘Not Buffalo Bills…’ – Analyst makes bold Angel Reese and Dream prediction for 2027 WNBA Finals ‘Awesome’: Yaxel Lendeborg names the Valkyries star who ‘looked just like Steph Curry’ in WNBA Finals

Quarterbacks There isn't much about the quarterback rankings that is going to surprise you. Josh Allen predictably comes in as our QB1, while Justin Herbert falls all the way to QB29 behind JJ McCarthy. item.title: Donte DiVincenzo Heard the Words Timberwolves Fans Have Been Waiting For
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Donte DiVincenzo already believed his comeback was progressing well. Hearing his surgeon agree gave him something the workouts alone couldn’t provide. In a new video released by the Minnesota Timberwolves , DiVincenzo visits orthopedic surgeon Dr. Martin O’Malley for an assessment of his recovery from a torn right Achilles tendon. The conversation offers encouragement for a guard determined to play this season. “We can easily say you’re on schedule, if not certainly ahead of schedule with your strength and all your numbers,” O’Malley told him. The discussion then turns to returning to basketball. “When this happened, the goal was to be back for this season,” O’Malley said. “That’s not even a question.” Apr 23, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Denver Nuggets guard Jamal Murray (27) works around Minnesota Timberwolves guard Donte DiVincenzo (0) in the first quarter at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images There is no announced return date. O’Malley emphasizes that the decision involves DiVincenzo and the team, with particular importance placed on when the guard feels ready and normal again. Still, the appointment gave DiVincenzo reassurance that his own assessment of his progress matched what his doctor was seeing. “This visit was a little bit more of just confirmation and confidence,” DiVincenzo explained. He described leaving with greater freedom to approach his next workout, trust his Achilles and move without constantly thinking about the injury. That is a meaningful development in a recovery he describes as being as much a mental challenge as a physical one. “I think half rehab is just a mental battle,” DiVincenzo said. Getting permission to progress, he explained, helps remove some of the fear attached to asking more of his body. He can push himself with greater confidence because the medical feedback supports how he feels. “Basically, his words match how I’m feeling,” he said. item.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Yankees rumors: New York could solve infield uncertainty by signing star player from Japan appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Once again, the New York Yankees ’ quest for their 28th World Series title fell short. For the second straight year, the Yankees defeated the Boston Red Sox in the AL Wild Card series. However, the same result followed in their AL Division Series (ALDS) matchup. In 2025, the Yankees lost to another division rival, the Toronto Blue Jays, in four games. This fall, a third division rival, the Tampa Bay Rays, swept New York in the ALDS. As the Bronx Bombers look to return to the Fall Classic for the first time since 2024, it’s clear that there are areas that need to be improved. One key spot is third base, where 2025 trade deadline pickup Ryan McMahon has failed to lock down the hot corner. Because of this, the Yankees are looking to upgrade the position. While appearing on Foul Territory, MLB insider Ken Rosenthal discussed the opening. Shared via X, formerly Twitter, Rosenthal expects New York to chase star Japanese third baseman Teruaki Sato this winter. "I expect the Yankees to be involved in the Sato market." @Ken_Rosenthal says the Japanese Triple Crown winner makes sense for New York, especially at third base. pic.twitter.com/r0XipGCGXp Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) November 2, 2026 “I expect the Yankees to be involved in the Sato market,” Rosenthal remarked on Monday morning. The Yankees have had success with Japanese stars before, most notably Hideki Matsui and former staff ace Masahiro Tanaka. However, New York has failed to attract overseas talent over the last few years, falling short in their pursuit of superstars like Shohei Ohtani and Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Will Sato prove to be different? If so, the Yankees could very well solve their third base woes. Arguably the top free agent hitter available, Sato could be the first Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB) player to win the MVP then leave for the MLB since Matsui joined New York in the mid-2000s. After winning NPB’s Triple Crown in 2026, it could be time for the 27-year-old to make his mark in the majors. Will he join the Bombers? Or will Sato ply his trade elsewhere in America? item.title: Everton Eye £33m Midfielder: Should Moyes Pay The Premium?
item.description: Everton Eye £33m Midfielder: Should Moyes Pay The Premium? Everton have made several changes to their midfield since Idrissa Gana Gueye left, with David Moyes looking to build a more balanced unit. Hayden Hackney arrived from Middlesbrough for a reported £16.5 million, while Christian Nørgaard joined from Arsenal for around £7 million. Merlin Röhl also arrived from Freiburg for £17 million, giving the manager more depth across central areas. Those additions have improved Moyes’ options, although Everton still have work to do after collecting 10 points from their opening eight Premier League matches. James Garner and Hackney have both contributed goals, including during the recent 3-1 Carabao Cup victory over Newcastle United . Their contributions offer encouragement, but neither removes the need for a midfielder who can sit in front of the defence, break up opposition attacks and protect the back four. Garner, contracted until 2030, remains an important part of Moyes’ plans, while Hackney represents a longer-term investment with his deal running until 2031. Nørgaard brings valuable experience, but his contract expires in 2028. A specialist defensive midfielder would give the younger pair more freedom to contribute further up the pitch without leaving Everton exposed during transitions. According to Goodison News, citing African outlet Africa Foot , Everton could revive their interest in Villarreal’s Pape Gueye in January. The 27-year-old Senegal international attracted attention after the 2026 World Cup and has continued his good form in Spain, scoring three goals in 10 La Liga appearances while featuring in the Champions League. Should Everton pay Villarreal’s £33m asking price? MADRID, SPAIN – OCTOBER 10: Pape Gueye of Villarreal CF in action during the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between Real Madrid and Villarreal CF at Estadio Santiago Bernabeu on October 10, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Reports suggest Everton considered a £23.3 million offer during the summer, but Villarreal value the midfielder at approximately £33.3 million. That difference presents a significant decision for Angus Kinnear and the recruitment team. From Everton’s perspective, paying the additional £10 million could make sense. Gueye offers the physical presence and defensive discipline that would allow Garner and Hackney to contribute further up the pitch. His arrival wouldn’t have to restrict Hackney’s progress; an established holding midfielder could give the young Englishman more freedom to develop his attacking game. However, Everton must ensure the fee reflects Gueye’s value to the team rather than simply meeting Villarreal’s demands.

item.title: Jack Campbell injury update from Lions on Monday offers more ‘positive’ news
item.description: The Detroit Lions have once again provided an update on injured linebacker Jack Campbell . The team announced on Monday afternoon that Campbell is still resting at the local hospital he was taken to after his scary neck injury on Sunday. The Lions did not provide specific details, but they did note that “preliminary indications are positive” for him. “Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital,” the Lions said . “Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time.” MORE: Vikings coach sends message after Jack Campbell’s scary injury How Jack Campbell suffered the injury Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell (47) is carted off the field after an injury during the fourth quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field. Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Campbell suffered his neck injury in the fourth quarter of the Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings. The former first-round pick came down with the injury while trying to make a tackle on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson. After staying down on the field for several minutes, Campbell was loaded onto a stretcher and carted off the field before being taken to a local hospital. What made the situation even scarier was the clear concern players had on their faces. Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson was brought to tears as he watched medical staff tend to his teammate. Dan Campbell, Lions react to Jack Campbell’s injury Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard check on linebacker Jack Campbell’s injury during the second half between Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Following the game, Lions head coach Dan Campbell revealed that the linebacker was alert and breathing as he was transported to the hospital. He urged everyone to send their thoughts and prayers to Campbell. “He’s breathing, he’s alert when he left. I know nothing further. Thoughts and prayers are with Jack. I would ask that everyone does the same,” Campbell said , per Lions beat reporter Brad Galli. The injury also led to an emotional postgame speech from the Lions head coach in the locker room after the 19-15 win over Minnesota. “That’s a gritty [expletive] win, man.” Dan Campbell’s postgame locker room speech was packed with emotions. item.title: Patrick Graham Reveals Turning Point for Steelers Defense
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers defense has been on a tear since the Week 4 loss to the Browns in Cleveland. The Steelers missed 14 tackles in that loss. Frustration was also mounting, as T.J. Watt took the head seat and chewed out defensive coordinator Patrick Graham . Graham has moved from the booth to the sideline since, and the defense has been playing lights out. The Steelers revenged that Week 4 loss on Sunday by crushing the Browns, 27-6. The defense had a whopping eight sacks on quarterback Deshaun Watson. Graham revealed on Monday that the loss to the Browns in Week 4 was the turning point for the defense and himself. Graham said he stared out the window listening to Amy Winehouse’s “Back to Black” on the bus ride back from Cleveland. It was a moment of deep reflection for him. “I had to learn how to trust them more. The input from the veteran players. Sometimes you don’t want to hear that,” Graham said. Pittsburgh Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham at training camp on July 29, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Heading into the bye week, the Steelers rank fourth in points per game allowed, sixth in EPA/play allowed, sixth in dropback EPA allowed, fifth in rushing EPA allowed, second in red zone defense and third in takeaways. The Steelers have also allowed just one second-half touchdown this year. The Steelers were historically bad in the fourth quarter last season. On a drive basis, the 2025 Steelers’ fourth-quarter defense ranked No. 32 in score rate per drive (60.4%), No. 32 in percentage of drives allowed to reach the red zone (40%), No. 31 in yards per drive allowed (36%) and No. 30 in punt rate forced (17%), according to Sharp Football . There have been 830 teams to play a season since 2000. The Steelers score rate of 60.4% ranked No. 826 of 830. In addition, Matt Williamson of Steelers.com posted this eye-opening stat. 174 of the Steelers’ 387 points against came in the fourth quarter, the most total points allowed in the fourth quarter since the 2020 Las Vegas Raiders. The Steelers sit atop the AFC North at 6-2 going into Week 9. Graham turning the defense back into an elite unit has been a big reason for the strong start. item.title: Sam Presti, Clay Bennett react to OKC Thunder retiring Russell Westbrook's No. 0 jersey
item.description: The Oklahoma City Thunder didn't take long to honor one of their greatest players ever. They have announced that Russell Westbrook will get his No. 0 jersey retired on Sunday, Feb. 7, against the New York Knicks . It will be part of NBC's Sunday Night Basketball slate. This felt fairly obvious to predict. Westbrook announced his NBA retirement this past offseason. He played a legendary 18 seasons in the league from 2008-26. The first 11 were with the Thunder — which were arguably his best years both on an individual and team level. Westbrook is one of the era-defining NBA superstars of the 2010s. He completely rewrote what the triple-double accolade meant. He was a one-time MVP winner and perennial All-Star and All-NBA member in his time in OKC. Alongside Kevin Durant, he co-starred in OKC's first title contender with a handful of deep playoff runs. Most of the Thunder franchise records still belong to Westbrook. Alongside Durant and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, those three are viewed as the biggest superstars in OKC's brief and successful franchise history. Thunder GM Sam Presti and owner Clay Bennett released statements on Westbrook's upcoming jersey retirement. Here's what both OKC figureheads had to say about the upcoming ceremony: Sam Presti "Many players make an impact but only great players leave a legacy. Russell Westbrook’s legacy was built both on the court and in the community. His mindset was relentless, his commitment deep. For all those reasons, Oklahomans consider him one of their own and his number will be raised to the rafters, in Oklahoma City forever." Clay Bennett "We are incredibly proud to retire Russell’s number. Russell made a lasting mark on the city and state during his time with the team, and his involvement in the community has endured long after. We are deeply grateful for his genuine care for the people of Oklahoma, and he will always be considered a member of the Oklahoma City community." item.title: Why Are The Pacers Dealing With So Many Hamstring Injuries Already?
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - MAY 11: Aaron Nesmith #23 and Tyrese Haliburton #0 of the Indiana Pacers celebrate in the second quarter against the Cleveland Cavaliers during Game Four of the Eastern Conference Semifinals at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on May 11, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) Getty Images INDIANAPOLIS – The Indiana Pacers have only played seven games in the 2026-27 season, yet the defining characteristic of their early-season games has already been decided: Poor health. Sunday night, the Pacers fell to the previously-winless Brooklyn Nets and scored just 90 points. Asked postgame about offensive struggles in the loss, head coach Rick Carlisle brought up the injury report. “We’re missing a lot of guys,” he said. “That makes it hard.” In that outing, the Pacers were without Tyrese Haliburton and Ivica Zubac, two of their top players and key starters. Their projected bench group was missing T.J. McConnell, Ben Sheppard, and Obi Toppin. Reserve forward Johnny Furphy, who suffered a torn ACL last season, is still sidelined . With six of their 17 players out, the Pacers don’t have as much high end talent and are missing much of their depth. That depth, plus Haliburton’s brilliance, made their winning ways possible in recent seasons. While a few of their injuries happened at clear moments in basketball settings (Furphy’s ACL, Zubac’s ankle after landing on a teammate, Toppin’s back avoiding a flying basketball during a shootaround), most of the team’s ailments are hamstring issues. Haliburton and McConnell are both currently out due to hamstring injuries. Quenton Jackson, Larry Nance Jr, and Aaron Nesmith have also missed time with hamstring problems for the Pacers this year. The Pacers changed their offseason approach to conditioning in an attempt to avoid this specific outcome. They didn’t make the playoffs last season and had a long summer, so the team designed a longer ramp-up approach to the 2026-27 season. “I think just the way we prepared through the summer, tracking our load management stuff,” Haliburton said of the differences from past offseasons. “Obviously dealt with a lot of soft tissue stuff over the last year and a half, two years. So just trying to manage all those things the correct way.” The Pacers could be without as many as 10 players tonight against the Atlanta Hawks. This is the second-straight season in which the opening weeks of the campaign have been defined by absences. And hamstrings have been the majority of those injuries. What, exactly, is the cause of this? The Pacers want to find out, especially after they tried to avoid this problem. “I guarantee you every team’s looking into it and studying it as best they can,” Carlisle said. item.title: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal: Havertz ends Gunners’ 14-year Anfield wait
item.description: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal: Havertz ends Gunners’ 14-year Anfield wait Kai Havertz’s first-half goal secured Arsenal a 1-0 victory over Liverpool, clinching their first Premier League win at Anfield since 2012. The German international put the visitors ahead in the 16th minute after capitalising on a defensive error from the Reds, who were unable to respond despite enjoying spells of attacking pressure. As it happened Iraola made one change to his starting XI from Liverpool’s previous Premier League outing, with Trey Nyoni replacing Ryan Gravenberch in midfield for his first league start. Mikel Arteta, meanwhile, made five changes to his side, including Kai Havertz starting ahead of Viktor Gyökeres. Arsenal enjoyed more possession in the opening stages, although neither side created much in front of goal. Cody Gakpo had an early chance for Liverpool but dragged his effort wide in the seventh minute. The Gunners broke the deadlock in the 16th minute after a misplaced pass from Alisson allowed them to regain possession. Declan Rice made an overlapping run around Noni Madueke before delivering a low cross into the box, where Havertz was waiting at the far post to finish. The goal appeared to bring the match to life, with the Reds beginning to apply more pressure in Arsenal’s half. Bradley Barcola looked particularly threatening down the left, but Liverpool could not find a way through the visitors’ defence. The hosts came closest to equalising when Florian Wirtz struck the crossbar with a free-kick in the 39th minute. Alexis Mac Allister then headed over from Milos Kerkez’s delivery three minutes later as the Reds continued to press. Iraola’s side kept pushing forward after the break, but the Gunners remained difficult to break down. The visitors had an opportunity of their own at the other end, with Christos Tzolis curling a first-time effort towards the bottom corner in the 73rd minute and forcing a fine save from Alisson. Tempers flared in the 78th minute following a confrontation involving several players. Alexis Mac Allister and Jurriën Timber were both shown yellow cards. Iraola made further changes in the closing stages as the hosts searched for a late equaliser, but Arteta’s squad held firm at the back. Liverpool pushed higher up the pitch and spent much of stoppage time in the visitors’ half, but they failed to find a breakthrough. They registered 17 shots and won seven corners, but not a single attempt was on target. The victory moved Arsenal three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the Premier League table with 24 points, while Liverpool remained fifth on 15 points.
